name: MO-07
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Eric Burlison running with large financial edge
Democrat Missi Hesketh raised only ~$50k with no outside support
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~96%
model.rationale: Burlison holds a seat with a 21-point Republican lean, has raised nearly $1.5 million against a Democratic challenger with about $50,000, and markets give him roughly a 96% win probability. With no polls or expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Burlison or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Missouri's seventh district is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a 21-point Republican partisan lean. Incumbent Eric Burlison is running for reelection after easily securing his party's nomination, and he enters the general election with a decisive financial advantage: about $1.5 million raised and nearly $1 million on hand, versus roughly $50,000 for Democrat Missi Hesketh.

Hesketh has drawn no outside spending support, and prediction markets price Burlison's chances at about 96%. With no public polling and no expert raters flagging the race as competitive, all available evidence points to a safe Republican hold, with the Libertarian candidate unlikely to alter the outcome.
